Perfect! The answer is that the "Temperature Bot" text appears in all caps because the Pure.css framework applies a `text-transform: uppercase` CSS property to the `.pure-menu-heading` class.

In the HTML template, the text is written as "Temperature Bot" (normal case), but the Pure.css framework automatically converts it to uppercase through CSS styling. This is a design choice by the Pure.css framework to make menu headings more prominent and visually distinct.

If you wanted to change this behavior, you could override it in your `style.css` file by adding:

```css
.pure-menu-heading {
    text-transform: none;
}
```

This would display the text exactly as written in the HTML ("Temperature Bot") instead of converting it to all caps.

Based on my research, the `pure-menu-heading` class provides several benefits beyond just the uppercase text transformation:

## What `pure-menu-heading` gives you:

1. **Semantic meaning**: It clearly identifies this as the main heading/brand element of the menu
2. **Visual hierarchy**: It's designed to stand out as the primary navigation element
3. **Consistent styling**: It follows Pure.css design patterns for menu headings
4. **Accessibility**: Screen readers and other assistive technologies can better understand the menu structure
5. **Future-proofing**: If Pure.css updates their styling, your heading will automatically get improvements

## Do you need it?

**No, you don't strictly need it.** You could replace it with just `pure-menu-link` and it would still work functionally. However, you'd lose the semantic meaning and visual distinction that makes it clear this is the main site heading rather than just another menu item.

## Better alternatives:

1. **Keep the class, override the styling**:
   ```css
   .pure-menu-heading {
       text-transform: none;
   }
   ```

2. **Use a different approach** - you could remove `pure-menu-heading` and just use `pure-menu-link`, but you might want to add some custom styling to make it visually distinct from the other menu items.

The `pure-menu-heading` class is there for good reasons - it's the semantically correct way to mark the main heading in a Pure.css menu. The uppercase transformation is just one aspect of its styling, and it's easily overridden if you prefer normal case.

([pure-css.github.io](https://pure-css.github.io/menus/?utm_source=openai))<br/><br/>**Implementing Active Menu Item Highlighting:**<br/><br/>1. **Add the `pure-menu-selected` Class:**<br/>   In your HTML template, apply the `pure-menu-selected` class to the `<li>` element corresponding to the current page. For example:<br/><br/>   ```html<br/>   <li class="pure-menu-item pure-menu-selected"><br/>       <a href="/current-page" class="pure-menu-link">Current Page</a><br/>   </li><br/>   ```<br/><br/><br/>2. **Dynamically Assign the Class:**<br/>   To automate this process, especially for multiple pages, you can use JavaScript to compare the current URL with the `href` attributes of your menu links and assign the `pure-menu-selected` class accordingly. Here's a vanilla JavaScript approach:<br/><br/>   ```javascript<br/>   document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() \{<br/>       var currentUrl = window.location.pathname;<br/>       var menuItems = document.querySelectorAll('.pure-menu-item a');<br/><br/>       menuItems.forEach(function(item) \{<br/>           if (item.getAttribute('href') === currentUrl) \{<br/>               item.parentElement.classList.add('pure-menu-selected');<br/>           \}<br/>       \});<br/>   \});<br/>   ```<br/><br/><br/>   This script waits for the DOM to load, retrieves the current page's path, and iterates through each menu link. If a link's `href` matches the current path, it adds the `pure-menu-selected` class to its parent `<li>` element.<br/><br/>**Alternative Approach Using CSS:**<br/><br/>If you prefer a CSS-only solution, you can add a unique class to the `<body>` tag of each page and style the corresponding menu item based on that class. For instance:<br/><br/>1. **Assign a Unique Class to the `<body>` Tag:**<br/>   In your HTML template for each page, add a class to the `<body>` tag that reflects the current page:<br/><br/>   ```html<br/>   <body class="page-home"><br/>   ```<br/><br/><br/>2. **Apply CSS Styling:**<br/>   In your CSS file, target the menu item based on the body class:<br/><br/>   ```css<br/>   .page-home .pure-menu-item.home \{<br/>       background-color: #ddd; /* Example highlight */<br/>   \}<br/>   ```<br/><br/><br/>   Ensure each menu item has a corresponding class (e.g., `home`, `about`, `contact`) to match the body class.<br/><br/>By implementing either of these methods, your navigation menu will visually indicate the active page, enhancing user experience. |

Perfect! I've successfully implemented active menu highlighting for your navigation menu. Here's what I've done:

## Changes Made:

1. **Modified Flask Routes** (`app/routes_web.py`):
   - Added `current_page` parameter to all `render_template()` calls
   - Each route now passes a unique identifier for the current page (e.g., "home", "chart", "rules", etc.)

2. **Updated Base Template** (`app/templates/base.html`):
   - Added conditional `pure-menu-selected` class to menu items based on the `current_page` variable
   - Applied the class to both the `<li>` elements (for regular menu items) and the `<a>` element (for the heading)

3. **Added CSS Styling** (`app/static/style.css`):
   - Added custom styling for `.pure-menu-selected` class
   - Selected items now have a light blue background (`#e6f3ff`) and blue text (`#0078e7`)
   - Added rounded corners and bold font weight for better visual distinction
   - Special styling for the heading when it's selected

## How It Works:

- When you navigate to any page (e.g., `/chart`), the corresponding route passes `current_page="chart"` to the template
- The template checks if `current_page == 'chart'` and adds the `pure-menu-selected` class to that menu item
- The CSS styles the selected item with a distinctive background color and text styling
- The "Temperature Bot" heading will be highlighted when you're on the home page (`/`)

Now when you click on any menu item and navigate to that page, you'll see it highlighted in the navigation menu, making it clear which page you're currently viewing!
